# Ezra Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 469v–470r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Then Darius the king issued a decree, and search was made in the house of the archives where the treasures were stored in Babylon. **2** And in Ecbatana, the citadel in the province of Media, a scroll was found on which this was written — a record:

**3** "In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king issued a decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt, the place where sacrifices are offered, and let its foundations be retained. Its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits, **4** with three rows of hewn stones and one row of new timber. Let the cost be paid from the royal treasury.

**5** And also let the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple at Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, be restored and brought back to the temple at Jerusalem, each to its place. You shall put them in the house of God."

**6** "Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates the officials in the province Beyond the River — keep away. **7** Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.

**8** Moreover, I make a decree regarding what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the rebuilding of this house of God: The full cost is to be paid to these people without delay from the royal revenue, the tribute of the province Beyond the River. **9** And whatever is needed — young bulls, rams, or lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, or oil, as the priests at Jerusalem require — let that be given to them day by day without fail, **10** that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

**11** Also I make a decree that if anyone alters this edict, a beam shall be pulled out of his house, and he shall be impaled on it, and his house shall be made a dunghill. **12** May the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who shall put out a hand to alter this, or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, make a decree; let it be done with all diligence."

**13** Then Tattenai, the governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates did with all diligence what Darius the king had ordered.

**14** And the elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. They finished their building by decree of the God of Israel and by decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia. **15** And this house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.

**16** And the people of Israel, the priests and the Levites, and the rest of the returned exiles, celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy. **17** They offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

**18** And they set the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God at Jerusalem, as it is written in the Book of Moses.

**19** On the fourteenth day of the first month, the returned exiles kept the Passover. **20** For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were clean. So they slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

**21** It was eaten by the people of Israel who had returned from exile, and also by everyone who had separated himself from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel. **22** And they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy, for the LORD had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, so that he aided them in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Ezra 6 is the great resolution — Cyrus's decree is found, Darius amplifies it, the temple is completed, and Passover is celebrated. The chapter moves from archive search (vv.1-2) through imperial decree (vv.3-12), obedient execution (v.13), construction and completion (vv.14-15), and finally dedication and festival (vv.16-22). The theological architecture is deliberate: the decree of "the God of Israel" stands first, followed by the decrees of three Persian kings (v.14), asserting that human empires execute divine will. The celebration of Passover at the chapter's end connects the return from Babylon to the exodus from Egypt — both are acts of divine liberation. The Aramaic section of the book (4:8-6:18) ends here, and Hebrew resumes with the Passover narrative, as if the return to the sacred language mirrors the return to the sacred land.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.12 — "caused his name to dwell there" vs. "chosen Jerusalem as the dwelling place for his Name"
- **EMET:** "who-has-caused-his-name to-dwell [shakkein] there"
- **LOGOS:** "who has caused his name to dwell there"
- **PNEUMA:** "who has chosen Jerusalem as the dwelling place for his Name"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "who has caused his name to dwell there" — the Aramaic follows Deuteronomic theology (*shikken shemeh tammah*). PNEUMA's expansion adds "chosen Jerusalem," which is theologically correct but not in this verse.

### V.21 — "separated himself from the uncleanness" vs. "separated themselves from the defilement"
- **EMET:** "who-had-separated-himself from-the-uncleanness [mittumat]"
- **LOGOS:** "separated himself from the uncleanness"
- **PNEUMA:** "separated themselves from the defilement"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "separated himself from the uncleanness" — maintaining the singular *ha-nivdal* and the technical term "uncleanness" (*tum'ah*) rather than the more general "defilement."

### V.22 — "king of Assyria"
- **All three** rendered this phrase faithfully; no significant disagreement. The council notes that this anachronistic title for the Persian king is theologically intentional and should be preserved without emendation.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
